speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. The association with an insect bite and your history of Crohn's disease raises suspicion for a specific type of inflammatory skin condition, but we must also rule out infection given your diabetes. Do you currently have any fever, chills, or systemic symptoms like joint pain or eye redness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a necrotic ulcer with purplish borders following minor trauma (ant bite), combined with your history of Crohn's disease and uveitis, strongly suggests Pyoderma Gangrenosum. To confirm this diagnosis of exclusion, have you noticed any similar skin lesions elsewhere on your body, and have you had any recent bowel symptoms or abdominal pain related to your Crohn's disease?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent trip to Wisconsin is a significant clue that might point toward a fungal infection rather than Pyoderma Gangrenosum, so I need to rule that out. I will request a biopsy of the ulcer edge to distinguish between inflammatory and infectious causes. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
